slot.brief: A two-parameter family of curves (parabolas/circles) is given; form the differential equation by differentiating and eliminating the arbitrary constants.

stem: The family of circles $x^2+y^2+2ax+2by=0$, where $a$ and $b$ are arbitrary constants, has differential equation

verdicts.working: Let p=y'. Differentiating gives x+yp+a+bp=0 and 1+p²+(y+b)y''=0. Eliminating a,b yields y+b=(x²+y²)/[2(y−xp)], so (x²+y²)y''+2(1+p²)(y−xp)=0.

working:
Set $p=y'$ and $q=y''$. Differentiating gives $F'=2x+2yp+2a+2bp=0$ and $F''=2+2p^2+2(y+b)q=0$. Hence $qb=-yq-(1+p^2)$ and $qa=-xq+p(1+p^2)$. Substituting in $qF=0$ gives $-q(x^2+y^2)+2(1+p^2)(xp-y)=0$, or $(x^2+y^2)y''+2(1+(y')^2)(y-xy')=0$.

Independent check: Let p=y'. Differentiating gives x+yp+a+bp=0 and 1+p²+(y+b)y''=0. Eliminating a,b yields y+b=(x²+y²)/[2(y−xp)], so (x²+y²)y''+2(1+p²)(y−xp)=0.
solution:
Differentiating twice and eliminating the arbitrary constants $a,b$ gives
$$
(x^2+y^2)y''+2(1+(y')^2)(y-xy')=0.
$$
Hence the required differential equation is (C).
